static_traits.name: Chen Yu
static_traits.family_status: Raised by Mother alone; Mother works two jobs at the same time; close relationship with Mother, but never discusses the Fear of spiders with her.
static_traits.social_status: Fear of spiders leads to significant avoidance, affecting relationships with others and daily activities; Social support mainly from Mother, close relationship but not yet sought help.
static_traits.medical_history: Has a condition that makes it impossible to go to high altitudes; No major physical illness; never received treatment or counseling for psychological issues before.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, highly cooperative; able to clearly describe Anxiety experiences and avoidance behaviors; harsh self-evaluation, frequently using 'should' phrasing and self-blame.

basic_info.main_problem: My Fear of spiders triggers intense Anxiety and dread, leading to avoidance behaviors. Every encounter with a spider causes extreme Anxiety and affects my daily life. I feel guilty and blame myself for not being brave enough.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because the fear of spiders significantly affects my daily life and brings suffering. I need to change my view of this whole 'fear' thing.
growth_experiences: Fear of spiders developed since childhood and persists to this day; every encounter with a spider brings extreme Anxiety and panic, with avoidance behaviors developing and affecting daily life.
Raised by Mother alone; Mother works two jobs to support the family, close relationship with Mother, but never talks with Mother about the Fear of spiders and the distress it causes.
Medical history: has a condition that makes it impossible to travel to high-altitude regions; apart from that, no significant physical illness.

core_beliefs: My problem: It is all my fault

special_situations.event: In places where spiders may appear, such as basements or garages
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I enter these places, I will very likely encounter spiders and be bitten or lose control
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids going into basements and garages; flees immediately at any spider-related clue
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: There is definitely a spider there; it will crawl on me or bite me, and I will panic out of control

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I show fear in front of others, it means I am very cowardly, and it is my fault
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Criticizes oneself with the inner self-instruction 'I should be braver', tries to suppress fear
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is my fault; I should be braver, then others will not look down on me

special_situations.event: Being invited by friends for a forest hike
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I go to the forest, I will be surrounded by spiders all over the woods and remain in intense fear
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Declining in advance or making excuses not to attend, to avoid possible encounters
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The forest is full of spiders; I will just be afraid all the time

special_situations.event: Feeling there was no effect after trying self-help Exposure techniques
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one attempt does not work, it proves I simply cannot do it / I am just cowardly
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing further attempts while intensifying Self-denial
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot change no matter what; I am too useless

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be understood and accepted, to be seen as a 'good enough' person even when afraid
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as cowardly, being negated or humiliated, fearing losing control in the face of Fear
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of safety by avoiding related situations
Directs blame toward oneself to avoid others' evaluation and relationship conflict

object_relations.self_representation: A self that is ashamed and not brave enough ('coward')
object_relations.object_representation: Others who may look down on or judge oneself

object_relations.self_representation: A child who should not trouble Mother
object_relations.object_representation: A hardworking, heavily burdened caregiver Mother

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes progressive preparation or exposure exercises for the upcoming forest hike
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If I cannot do it I will seem even more cowardly, and others will look down on me (anticipating being judged through transference)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First empathize with and normalize the fear, with a gentle and slow tone; reduce evaluative wording, emphasize safety and controllability; use open questions to guide the client to turn attention from 'self-blame' toward concrete feasible small-step goals.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about whether to seek support from Mother and express one's Fear
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If telling Mother adds to her burden, it shows I am not sensible
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Keep a gentle, non-blaming tone; first acknowledge the motive of being considerate toward Mother; then use exploratory Questioning to distinguish 'caring' from 'avoiding help-seeking', invite evaluation of the pros and cons of different communication styles, and offer small, retractable sharing options.

manifestations: Fear causes extensive avoidance of basements, garages, outdoor hiking and other situations
Constantly tense, hard to relax, always worries about encountering spiders
Although close to Mother, has not yet confided Fear and distress to Mother

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently using self-Demands like 'I should be braver' to judge oneself
Taking society's expectations of 'bravery' as the standard for self-judgment without digesting them

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on.
manifestations: Harshly scrutinizing one's own Fear and blaming oneself: 'It is all my fault'
Expressing cautiously in sessions, negating oneself first, worrying about being judged as cowardly

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: When afraid and tense, not seeking help outward but turning energy into self-blame and withdrawal
Choosing not to seek help from Mother so as 'not to trouble others'

positive_force: Actively seeking counseling, willing to change
Able to identify and express one's automatic thoughts and emotions
Close relationship with Mother, potential support resources available
Has tried self-help Exposure techniques, showing some willingness to act
Can practice more compassionate self-talk and feel relief
negative_force: Catastrophic/predictive thinking about danger, exaggerating the threat of spiders
Widespread avoidance behaviors reinforcing Fear responses
Self-blame and 'should' phrasing lead to shame and guilt
Not yet actively seeking support from significant others, bearing it alone
Overgeneralizing from one ineffective attempt, lowering Self-efficacy

target_behavior.behavior: Intense fear and panicked avoidance when encountering spiders
antecedent: Enters places where spiders may be, such as basements and garages
Thinks about scenes such as hiking in the forest where spiders may be
target_behavior.core_reason: A childhood-formed exaggerated association of spider dangerousness and the catastrophic belief 'will be bitten / lose control' maintain the fear response
target_behavior.function: Escapes intense fear to quickly restore a subjective sense of safety
target_behavior.consequence: Frequent avoidance affects daily life and relationships; the fear is maintained long-term

target_behavior.behavior: Harsh self-critical self-talk centered on 'should be braver / It is all my fault'
antecedent: Reflecting on one's reactions after Fear and fleeing
Talking about failed self-help exposure attempts
Facing others' invitations to occasions where spiders may appear
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjecting the external norm of 'bravery' as the standard of self-worth, and Turning shame and frustration against the self in an attempt to control
target_behavior.function: Tries to prompt change or maintain a sense of self-control through self-blame
target_behavior.consequence: Intensifying guilt and shame, further raising Anxiety and reducing willingness to face situations
